misleading_risk: Low if built as refined, but three real risks. (1) The text is author-written and unverified, so a "Works with" block can read as a claim the site endorses. The existing Community legend already says listing is no validation, and the block is no different from the existing author-written summary and description. Do not let anyone but the app owners write the real values. (2) The seed drafts must not be filled from guesswork. They may only quote facts the READMEs state: CellTracksColab 'CSV or XML' and 'does not yet support track merging or splitting', NucleiSky pixel size in um/px and similarity transform only, GuessTheCondition .tif/.tiff in condition/repeat folders. NucleiSky accepting OME-Zarr is supported by docs/2D/data_preparation.md and zarr==3.2.1 in requirements.txt, but the owner should confirm it for the desktop app. (3) Contradiction: GuessTheCondition/README.md says 'Apple-silicon Macs are supported; Intel Macs are not', yet the built page offers 'Intel 179 MB .pkg'. A free-text limitation placed below the download tiles would be read after the click, and one placed beside an Intel button would visibly contradict it. The site must not resolve this itself. Flag it to the owners: drop the Intel installer or state the limitation. Also avoid the label 'Works with', which collides with the existing 'Works in' (napari, Fiji, QuPath pills in details_list and the App Centre filter). A visible 'Not stated by the author' is not misleading (same precedent as License 'Not stated'). It would be if shown for Limitations, where it could read as 'none known'.
refined_proposal:
Build the core, drop the extras.

1. Schema (schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json, same pattern as `quickstart`): three optional arrays of plain-text strings, `inputs`, `outputs`, `limitations`, 1-4 items each, 5-160 characters per item, with descriptions telling the author to give one short phrase per item and to use docs_url for the rest. No `example_data` (outside this gap). Rollout order: publish the site schema first, because additionalProperties is false and the site validates every app manifest against its own schema. The initialiser (LabConstrictor_streamlit) is NOT a blocker: its schemas/ copy has identical properties today, the new fields are optional, and it keeps producing valid manifests. Sync its copy and form later.

2. New pure module scripts/lcsite/pages_facts.py, with page_app gaining one line (`p.add(facts_block(app))` between the header and get_section; page_app is about 20 lines, pages_apps.py is 208 of 300).
   - `io_expected(section)` is False only for section "testing". It is the single rule. Used by both the page and the warning, it covers Demo and Playground without a per-kind exemption table.
   - `missing_io(manifest, section)` returns the missing field names, read with `in` or optional_list, never .get with a default.
   - `facts_block(app)` renders one h2 ("Data and results" or similar, sentence case) holding a `<dl class="lc-facts">`, reusing the existing CSS from details_list (no new CSS). Rows are 'Accepts' (inputs), 'Produces' (outputs) and 'Limitations', each item escaped with text.esc. Use the label 'Accepts', not 'Works with', to avoid the collision with 'Works in'.
   - Put Limitations in this same block above 'Get it', not under 'Using it' as the auditor proposed. Benchmark 2B item 4 puts 'relevant limitations' with the data types in the decision area, and the GuessTheCondition Intel case shows why: a limitation below the download is read after the click.
   - Absent handling: for non-testing apps a missing inputs or outputs row shows the plain text 'Not stated by the author'. A missing Limitations row is simply omitted, because 'Not stated' there would look like a defect and 'none' may be true. For testing-section apps every absent row is omitted, and the whole block is omitted if the author wrote nothing.

3. Warnings: in catalogue.resolve, when `missing_io` is non-empty append one warning per app, for example 'inputs, outputs not stated: the page shows "Not stated by the author"'. It never unlists the app (icon-warning precedent, catalogue.py:82). It reaches build/problems.md, the fetch log, and every submitter through scripts/submit_app.py:58 (`app["warnings"]` become the issue comment's warning lines). That last route is the real enforcement point for external authors and needs no new code. Warnings do not open issues (publish.yml only greps the left-out-apps section), so six standing warnings are noise in problems.md but do not spam anyone.

4. Docs: add the 'facts block' pattern to DESIGN.md in the same change (AGENTS.md says add the pattern first). Add one sentence and one example line to content/submit.md. Add a template app-manifest guide mention later.

5. Seed drafts: fill seed/manifests/*.yaml only with phrases taken from each README and cite the source line in the PR. Leave out the GuessTheCondition Intel limitation until the owners decide, and report the contradiction to them. The real values belong in each app's own labconstrictor-app.yaml; only LabConstrictor-Playground has one today, and the other five are previewed via `--manifest-dir seed/manifests`.

6. Tests: schema accepts present fields and rejects an empty array, 5 items, an over-long item and a non-string; facts_block escapes '<' in an item; absent in the apps section gives 'Not stated by the author' plus a warning; absent in the testing section gives no block and no warning; Limitations absent gives no row. check_site's escaping check already scans every manifest string, so it covers the new fields.

Optional one-liner, outside the gap: add inputs and outputs to cards.search_text (cards.py:123) so that 'TrackMate' or 'OME-Zarr' finds the app.

Dropped from the auditor's proposal: the per-kind exemptions, the matching initialiser and form changes, `example_data`, and Limitations under 'Using it'.
evidence:
Gap is real (checked built HTML, not just code). I extracted headings from site/apps/*/index.html for all six apps. Every page has only: h1, Get it (Windows/macOS/Linux, Notebooks), About, Using it, All downloads, How to install, Details. Keyword search for 'Works with', 'Produces', 'Limitation', 'CSV', 'TIFF', 'OME' found nothing on any page. The only hit was the word 'pixel' in NucleiSky's About ('Instead of relying on pixel intensity...'). The page code agrees: scripts/lcsite/pages_apps.py page_app lines 189-207 emit header, get_section, About, screenshots, using_section, downloads and install help, then details_list. Details has 'Works in' (programs only, via works_in()), which is not data formats. Screenshot (scratchpad/skeptic-g1/nucleisky-desk.png, 1280x800) shows the header followed directly by the Get it tiles, with no data statement. Offsets for /apps/nucleisky/: #get at y=383 desktop and 444 mobile. A block of about 2-3 rows adds roughly 100-150px, so the Linux/Windows buttons stay in the first desktop viewport.

Schema gap: schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json has additionalProperties false at the top and no inputs/outputs/limitations. I ran validate.check on seed/manifests/NucleiSky.yaml plus an `inputs` list and got: 'Additional properties are not allowed ('inputs' was unexpected)'. The existing free-text `description` (maxLength 2000, schema line 18) can already hold such prose, but it renders under About after Get it, unstructured, so it cannot meet 'directly under the summary'. The six descriptions give inputs and outputs only partly: CellTracksColab 'tracking results (for example from TrackMate)', GuessTheCondition 'accuracy against chance and a confusion matrix'. NucleiSky, VLab4Mic, Demo and Playground state neither.

Facts are in READMEs/docs, confirmed by reading them: CellTracksColab/README.md lines 152-168 (Required File Format: 'CSV or XML files' / 'CSV files') and line 248 ('does not yet support track merging or splitting'). NucleiSky/README.md line 79-82 (Two Golden Rules: pixel size um/px, segmentation quality); docs/limitations.md (similarity transform only, no deformable registration, 2D input strictly 2D); docs/2D/data_preparation.md lines 50-58 (TIFF/OME-TIFF recommended, Zarr/OME-Zarr accepted); docs/exports.md (aligned .tif / .zarr, transform JSON, overlay PNG). requirements.txt line 10 has zarr==3.2.1. GuessTheCondition/README.md line 29-41 (.tif/.tiff, condition/repeat folders) and line 49 ('Apple-silicon Macs are supported; Intel Macs are not'). Playground/README.md line 48 ('Honest limits').

Contradiction found: the built /apps/guessthecondition/ macOS tile offers 'Intel 189 MB .pkg' (release assets include macos x86_64), against the README's 'Intel Macs are not' supported. Evidence for showing limitations next to the download, and for the site not making the call itself.

Rule checks: AGENTS.md 'Optional manifest fields may be absent (checked explicitly with optional_list or in)' and the License 'Not stated' precedent (pages_apps.py details_list) support the 'Not stated by the author' design. Warnings: catalogue.py:82 (icon warning, never unlists). scripts/submit_app.py:58 turns app["warnings"] into the submission-issue comment. publish.yml lines 65-74 open issues only for left-out apps, not warnings. check_site.author_strings (lines 100-120) scans every manifest string, so new fields are escape-checked automatically. Only LabConstrictor-Playground has a labconstrictor-app.yaml in its repo; the other five are previewed from seed/manifests. LabConstrictor_streamlit/schemas has the same property list as the site schema (diffed), and its form only builds name, summary, kind, hosts and description, so it need not change for validity.

Not verified: I did not run the build or tests with the change (read-only audit). I did not verify that the NucleiSky desktop installer can actually read OME-Zarr beyond the README, the docs and the bundled zarr requirement. The 100-150px layout estimate is not measured with a prototype.
